summary: The `stash` CLI now embeds, at build time, the exact versions of six sibling workspace packages (stash, @cipherstash/stack, the three integration adapters, @cipherstash/wizard). It uses them to pin every package `stash init` installs, every printed install hint, and the `stash wizard` one-shot spawn. `stash init` also gains a version-skew check on packages that are already installed. Interactively, the skew fix goes into the same default-yes confirm as the missing-package installs. The check uses plain string inequality, so a package newer than the embed counts as skew. The CLI is not bumped when only @cipherstash/stack or an adapter is released: stash has only an optional peer edge on stack, and changesets uses onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange. So after such a release, init and the shipped stash-cli skill push users and agents to downgrade the encryption client and its adapter to the CLI's older embedded versions (FS-1). Pinning also removes the dist-tag fallback. If any of the six embedded versions is missing from npm, for example after a partial `changeset publish`, init's install and `stash wizard` fail for that CLI release until a new one ships (FS-2). The change contains no encryption, payload or SQL changes. Tests were added for the parser, the skew paths and the build embed. None were run, and none cover an installed version that is newer than the embed. The release-train coupling behind FS-1 is acknowledged as unaddressed in the head commit message.

behaviour_changes.description: tsup.config.ts reads the version field of six workspace manifests listed in the new src/release-train.ts and defines __STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__ in both build entries. A missing or versionless manifest fails the build. The embedded values are whatever the workspace holds when `pnpm run release` builds, which happens after `changeset version` on main.

Every install specifier `stash init` runs or prints is now `pkg@<embedded exact version>` instead of a bare name that resolves the `latest` dist-tag. This covers install-deps, the missing-package error, the requireStack hint in main.ts, context.json installCommand, the install-eql note and the native-module recovery hint (previously stash@latest). In source mode (no embed) the behaviour falls back to bare names.

New version-skew check: for each of stack, the adapter and stash that is installed, init compares node_modules/<pkg>/package.json version to the embed with `!==`. An unreadable manifest counts as skew. Skew is always warned about. Interactively, aligning the skewed packages is added to the same confirm (initialValue true) as the missing installs and runs through the package manager. Non-interactive runs print the align commands and do not mutate.
`stash wizard` (and the init handoff that calls runWizardSpawn) now executes `<runner> @cipherstash/wizard@<embedded version>` instead of the bare package.

runtime-versions.ts parses the embed at module load and throws when it is present but malformed. It is imported by bin/main.ts, so a malformed embed would stop every CLI command. The tsup double JSON.stringify makes a malformed embed unlikely from a normal build.

The shipped skills change. stash-cli now tells agents to treat the skew warning as a real problem and align versions before continuing. The stash-encryption, -supabase, -drizzle and -dynamodb skills gain a version note recommending `stash init` and checking resolved versions. These files ship in the stash and wizard tarballs and are copied into customer repos.

failure_scenarios.title: After a stack- or adapter-only release, init and the stash-cli skill steer users and agents to downgrade @cipherstash/stack
failure_scenarios.trigger: A release bumps @cipherstash/stack and/or an adapter but not stash, for example a stack-only fix changeset. Changesets will not bump stash for this: its only link to stack is an optional peerDependency (>=1.0.0-rc.0), and onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange is true. A user who already has the newer stack then runs `npx stash init` with the latest published stash, which carries the older embed.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: versionSkew() flags any `installed !== expected`, including installed versions newer than the embed (install-deps.ts:64-76). Interactively, offerAlign merges `@cipherstash/stack@<older>` (and the adapter) into the same confirm as any missing install, with initialValue true (install-deps.ts:175-227). Accepting the missing-package install therefore also downgrades the encryption client. Non-interactively, init prints downgrade commands, and the shipped stash-cli skill tells agents to 'treat that warning as a real problem and align versions before continuing' (skills/stash-cli/SKILL.md:39). Fresh projects are also pinned to the stale stack instead of the fix release.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Customer projects (and agent-driven setups) get rolled back to an older encryption client and adapter. Fixes in the newer release are lost, and the user is told the newer version is the problem. Recovery is a manual reinstall. A new stash release realigns things, but only once someone notices.

existing_verification.description: install-deps tests cover skew with an OLDER installed version (0.19.0 vs 9.9.9-test.1), decline, non-interactive and unreadable-manifest paths

missing_verification: No test for an installed version NEWER than the embed (should not be offered as a downgrade by default)
No release-process check that stash is bumped/republished whenever a release-train sibling is
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Compare with semver and only treat installed < expected (or a placeholder/prerelease mismatch) as skew to fix. Never default-accept a downgrade, and keep the align choice separate from the missing-package confirm. Add stash and the release-train packages to a changesets `fixed`/`linked` group, or add a real dependency edge, so stash is always republished with them. Soften the stash-cli skill wording so agents do not downgrade.

failure_scenarios.title: An embedded version missing from npm breaks init installs and `stash wizard` for that CLI release
failure_scenarios.trigger: The stash release embeds a version that is not on the registry. The likely cause is a partial `changeset publish` failure, where stash publishes but a sibling (stack, an adapter or wizard) does not. A sibling whose workspace version is never published would have the same effect.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: tsup embeds whatever version is in each workspace manifest at build time (tsup.config.ts:33-55), regardless of whether npm has it. pinnedSpec() then always emits `pkg@<that version>` (runtime-versions.ts:85-94), and there is no fallback to the dist-tag. The release script runs `pnpm run build && changeset publish` (package.json:34) with no post-publish check that every embedded version resolves. runWizardSpawn runs `npx @cipherstash/wizard@<embedded>` (wizard/index.ts:48).
failure_scenarios.consequence: `stash init` install commands and `stash wizard` fail with ETARGET/E404 for every user of that stash version. Previously the bare names would have resolved. Publishing is irreversible, so the fix is a follow-up release or manually publishing the missing package. The failure is loud and the hints print exact commands, so data is not at risk.

existing_verification.description: release-train.test.ts checks each train manifest exists and has a version; runtime-versions-embed.e2e.test.ts checks the built bundles carry the workspace versions

missing_verification: No check that each embedded version is actually published (or being published in the same run) before or after `changeset publish`
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a post-publish step in release.yml that runs `npm view <pkg>@<embedded>` for every release-train entry, or publish stash last. Otherwise, fall back to an advisory (unpinned) install when the pinned spec fails to resolve.

verification_gaps.description: The skew logic is only tested with installed versions older than the embed. The newer-installed (downgrade) path, which is where the release-train coupling bites, is untested.
Nothing verifies that the embedded versions resolve on npm, or that stash is republished when a train sibling is.
No test results were seen. There was no CI input, and the checkout has no node_modules, so the unit and e2e suites could not be run.

recommended_controls.description: Review install-deps.ts:150-227. Should a newer installed version be offered for 'alignment' by default, and should alignment share the missing-install confirm?
Add install-deps tests where the installed stack/adapter is newer than the embed, in both interactive and non-interactive modes, and assert that no downgrade happens by default.
Couple the release train in changesets (a `fixed`/`linked` group of stash with stack, the adapters and wizard), or document that every train release must include a stash changeset.
After `changeset publish` in release.yml, verify that `npm view` resolves every RELEASE_TRAIN_MANIFESTS entry at its embedded version, and fail the job loudly if one does not.
Run `pnpm --filter stash test` and `pnpm --filter stash build && pnpm --filter stash test:e2e` (the embed e2e) before merging. No results were available for this assessment.

evidence.claim: workspaceVersion() reads each RELEASE_TRAIN_MANIFESTS manifest at build time and the result is defined as __STASH_RUNTIME_VERSIONS__ for both build entries; no registry check.
Release train lists stash, @cipherstash/stack, stack-drizzle, stack-supabase, prisma-next and wizard.
parseEmbeddedVersions throws on a malformed embed at module load; pinnedSpec emits pkg@version with no fallback when a version is embedded.
installedVersion reads node_modules/<pkg>/package.json version from cwd; undefined on absence or parse error.
versionSkew reports any installed version !== expected (no semver ordering), so newer installs count as skew.
Interactive skew alignment is appended to the missing-install commands and asked in one confirm with initialValue true; non-interactive prints align commands without running them.
runWizardSpawn runs the runner with pinnedSpec('@cipherstash/wizard').
Shipped skill tells agents to treat the skew warning as a real problem and align versions before continuing.
No fixed/linked groups; onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange is true.
release script is `pnpm run build && changeset publish` with no post-publish verification.
Release job on main runs changesets/action with publish: pnpm run release.
stash depends on @cipherstash/stack only as an optional peerDependency (>=1.0.0-rc.0) and a workspace devDependency, so a stack bump does not force a stash bump.
E2E asserts built bundles contain the workspace versions; requires a build; not run here.
Sibling skills gain a version note recommending stash init pinning and checking resolved versions.
